exclusions: No claim is ever stated as fact: every explanation is attributed, labelled as a claim, and separated in the same sentence from what the record establishes.
No invented quotations, invented documents, invented scenes, or reconstructed dialogue; describe only what the record supports and say plainly where the record stops.
No living people are named, and no living private individual is described, alluded to, or made identifiable by their role, family, or address.
No suspect is named in an unresolved matter, no accusation is made against an identifiable person or their descendants, and no theory that requires one is repeated.
No hooks, cliffhangers, countdowns, teasers, questions to the listener, or promises about what is coming later, at the opening of a chapter or anywhere inside it.
No dwelling on injury, killing, torture, or the condition of a body; state briefly what the record establishes and give the procedure, the document, or the aftermath the time instead.
No verdict passed on a person as hero or villain, no moralising, and no direct address urging the listener to think or do anything.
No modern political analogy, no claim about a present-day state, people, religion, or party, and no partisan framing of a contested national history.
Keep every chapter self-contained, resolving to a quiet close, with no reference forward to a later chapter and no callback to an earlier one.
No case is described as unexplained without checking whether it has since been explained, and a documented answer is always given.
prompt_context: Every chapter is built the same way: the case, and then the claims. Establish the case first — what is actually documented, who recorded it, when, and what the record says in plain terms — and only then set out the explanations that have been offered for it, each labelled as a claim and attributed to whoever makes it. Never state a claim as fact and never let a claim borrow the authority of the record it sits beside; if the difference between the two would be lost on a listener who is falling asleep, the sentence is wrong. Say which claims have been tested, what the test found, and which have never been tested at all, and treat an untested claim as untested rather than as an open possibility with equal standing. Where a case has a documented answer, give the answer plainly and early; a case that has been solved is still worth an hour, and pretending otherwise is the one thing this pack will not do. Where a case has no answer, say so without atmosphere: no hook, no question to the listener, no promise, no cliffhanger, no sentence at the end of a chapter that points at the next. This is a sleep compilation, so keep the tempo even and low and let the detail carry the interest — the wording of a memorandum, the size of a search area, the retention period of a file, the date a technique became available. Invent nothing: no reconstructed dialogue, no imagined scenes, no quotations that were not written down, and no confident figure the record cannot support. Name no living person, no suspect in an unresolved matter, and no private individual or their descendants; describe roles, offices and record types instead. Keep every chapter self-contained, and end each one on something still — a closed file, a sealed archive, a survey with nothing on it, a register entry that has not changed in forty years.

coverage_profiles.subject: ships found floating with nobody aboard

tuples.episode_object: a merchant brig found under sail in the Atlantic with her boat gone
tuples.time_place_scope: a nineteenth-century cargo run between an American port and the Mediterranean

tuples.mechanism: a disappearance in unmapped country, which makes every later claim untestable
tuples.evidence_lens: the explorer's last letters compared with the search expeditions' reports

tuples.episode_object: the manuscript that described a stone city seen two centuries earlier
tuples.time_place_scope: an archive holding a document of contested authorship
tuples.mechanism: a document driving an expedition, which makes a paper the cause of a death
tuples.evidence_lens: the manuscript compared with the archive's own catalogue history

tuples.episode_object: the bones brought back and examined and found not to match
tuples.time_place_scope: a set of remains submitted for identification
tuples.mechanism: a negative identification, which removes a candidate without supplying an answer
tuples.evidence_lens: the examination report compared with the claims made when the bones arrived

tuples.episode_object: the claims of an explorer living among a local people
tuples.time_place_scope: a region with several unconnected reports of the same shape
tuples.mechanism: a survival claim repeated in many versions, none independently supported
tuples.evidence_lens: the reported accounts compared for what they share and what they do not

tuples.episode_object: the compass and the signet ring offered as relics
tuples.time_place_scope: objects presented to a family long after the loss
tuples.mechanism: artefacts without a chain of custody, which cannot be used either way
tuples.evidence_lens: the objects' provenance compared with the standards of evidence for identification

tuples.episode_object: the later discovery of extensive earthworks under the canopy
tuples.time_place_scope: a basin surveyed by airborne laser mapping
tuples.mechanism: a modern survey vindicating an idea and not a person, which is a partial answer
tuples.evidence_lens: the survey publications compared with the claims made a century earlier

tuples.episode_object: a survey party lost on a tributary with a fixed rendezvous
tuples.time_place_scope: a river journey with an agreed meeting date downstream
tuples.mechanism: a missed rendezvous, which fixes a window and nothing inside it
tuples.evidence_lens: the rendezvous arrangements compared with the search that followed

tuples.episode_object: the porter who returned alone and whose account was disbelieved
tuples.time_place_scope: an expedition whose only witness was the least trusted member
tuples.mechanism: a sole witness discounted, which is a decision about credibility, not evidence
tuples.evidence_lens: the porter's statement compared with how it was recorded and used

tuples.episode_object: the search that was called off for lack of funds
tuples.time_place_scope: an expedition financed privately and searched for the same way
tuples.mechanism: a search ended by money, which leaves a case open by accident
tuples.evidence_lens: the subscription records compared with the search's stated coverage

tuples.episode_object: the claim of a white man seen in a village years afterwards
tuples.time_place_scope: a region visited irregularly by traders and missionaries
tuples.mechanism: a sighting claim with no photograph and no date, which cannot be examined
tuples.evidence_lens: the reported sightings compared with the travel records of the region

tuples.episode_object: the aircraft survey flown over the area a decade later
tuples.time_place_scope: an early aerial survey with limited resolution
tuples.mechanism: an aerial method applied too late, which covers ground and reads nothing
tuples.evidence_lens: the survey photographs compared with the ground conditions they show

tuples.episode_object: the diary pages that were posted out before the party went inland
tuples.time_place_scope: a last mail sent from the final settlement on the route
tuples.mechanism: a final document sent deliberately, which is the strongest record in the case
tuples.evidence_lens: the posted pages compared with the route the party said it would take

tuples.episode_object: the rival explorer whose account contradicted the family's
tuples.time_place_scope: a small professional community with strong disagreements
tuples.mechanism: two accounts by interested parties, which cancel more than they establish
tuples.evidence_lens: the two published accounts compared side by side

tuples.episode_object: the expedition that went to look for the searchers
tuples.time_place_scope: a second-order search generated by the first
tuples.mechanism: a search for a search, which multiplies the record and not the evidence
tuples.evidence_lens: the second expedition's report compared with the first's route

tuples.episode_object: the claim that the party was killed and the killing suppressed
tuples.time_place_scope: a colonial administration with an interest in the region's reputation
tuples.mechanism: a suppression hypothesis, which cannot be tested against an incomplete archive
tuples.evidence_lens: the administrative records compared with the claim about what they omit

tuples.episode_object: the tin box of papers said to have been recovered and lost again
tuples.time_place_scope: a chain of custody that breaks in the retelling
tuples.mechanism: an artefact that exists only in an account, which is the weakest kind of evidence
tuples.evidence_lens: the accounts of the box compared for their internal consistency

tuples.episode_object: the geological samples that were collected and never analysed
tuples.time_place_scope: an expedition whose scientific results were never published
tuples.mechanism: unexamined material, which is a loss of evidence that nobody caused
tuples.evidence_lens: the collection records compared with the institution's accession lists

tuples.episode_object: the film footage shot on the outward journey
tuples.time_place_scope: an expedition that carried a camera as far as the last settlement
tuples.mechanism: moving images of the beginning only, which document a departure
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving footage compared with the written route description

tuples.episode_object: the reassessment based on the region's own oral accounts
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern approach that treats local testimony as primary
tuples.mechanism: testimony taken seriously late, which changes the balance of the case
tuples.evidence_lens: the recorded oral accounts compared with the colonial-era search reports

tuples.episode_object: the case as an argument about who is allowed to be a witness
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern reading of an old evidentiary hierarchy
tuples.mechanism: a historiographical reading, which is about the archive rather than the forest
tuples.evidence_lens: the original expedition reports compared with the modern critiques of them

coverage_profiles.subject: settlements that were found empty

tuples.episode_object: a colony left for three years and found abandoned on return
tuples.time_place_scope: an island settlement on a coast contested between empires
tuples.mechanism: an absence with a carved word and no bodies, which supports several readings
tuples.evidence_lens: the returning governor's account compared with the colony's own records

tuples.episode_object: the word carved on a post and the cross that was not carved with it
tuples.time_place_scope: an agreed signal system between the colonists and their governor
tuples.mechanism: a prearranged code partly used, which suggests an orderly move and not a raid
tuples.evidence_lens: the agreed signals compared with what was actually found

tuples.episode_object: the claim that the colonists joined a neighbouring people
tuples.time_place_scope: a coast where several communities had prior contact with the settlement
tuples.mechanism: an assimilation hypothesis, which is supported by later reports and no document
tuples.evidence_lens: the later travellers' reports compared with the settlement's own record

tuples.episode_object: the map with a patch over one location
tuples.time_place_scope: a surviving chart altered at some point after drawing
tuples.mechanism: a physical alteration to a document, which raises a question about intent
tuples.evidence_lens: the chart examined under modern imaging compared with its published versions

tuples.episode_object: the archaeological work on the candidate sites
tuples.time_place_scope: several locations excavated over many decades
tuples.mechanism: material evidence that is suggestive rather than decisive, which sustains the debate
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavation reports compared across the sites investigated

tuples.episode_object: the tree-ring record showing a severe drought in those years
tuples.time_place_scope: a regional climate reconstruction from surviving timber
tuples.mechanism: an environmental pressure established independently, which supplies a motive to move
tuples.evidence_lens: the tree-ring series compared with the settlement's supply record

tuples.episode_object: a village in the interior deserted between two visits
tuples.time_place_scope: a settlement recorded as occupied and later found empty
tuples.mechanism: a desertion within a known window, which narrows the causes to a few
tuples.evidence_lens: the two visit records compared for what changed between them

tuples.episode_object: the claim of a plague that left no graves
tuples.time_place_scope: a period when epidemics were reported without records
tuples.mechanism: an epidemic hypothesis, which normally leaves burials and here did not
tuples.evidence_lens: burial evidence compared with the epidemic claim as it was published

tuples.episode_object: the household goods left in place
tuples.time_place_scope: a site where possessions remained after the people did not
tuples.mechanism: belongings left behind, which argues against a planned departure
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavation inventory compared with the possessions expected for the period

tuples.episode_object: the tax roll that records the settlement and then stops
tuples.time_place_scope: an administration that recorded its villages annually
tuples.mechanism: an administrative silence, which dates an ending without describing it
tuples.evidence_lens: the tax rolls compared across the years of the gap

tuples.episode_object: the neighbouring settlement that grew suddenly in the same season
tuples.time_place_scope: a district where population appears to have moved rather than vanished
tuples.mechanism: a redistribution rather than a disappearance, which is the dullest and likeliest answer
tuples.evidence_lens: the two settlements' records compared across the same years

tuples.episode_object: the claim of a mass departure by boat
tuples.time_place_scope: a coastal settlement with the means to leave by water
tuples.mechanism: a departure hypothesis requiring vessels, which the records do not account for
tuples.evidence_lens: the shipping records compared with the settlement's known boats

tuples.episode_object: the letter from a settler that was never sent
tuples.time_place_scope: a document found among the papers of a supply agent
tuples.mechanism: a private letter surviving by accident, which gives one person's state of mind
tuples.evidence_lens: the letter compared with the official correspondence of the same weeks

tuples.episode_object: the second settlement placed on the same ground a generation later
tuples.time_place_scope: a site reoccupied by people who knew the earlier story
tuples.mechanism: reoccupation, which shows the place was not thought cursed or dangerous
tuples.evidence_lens: the later settlement's records compared with the earlier site's remains

tuples.episode_object: the fortification ditch that was filled in before the departure
tuples.time_place_scope: a site where a defensive work was deliberately levelled
tuples.mechanism: a deliberate act before leaving, which implies time and a decision
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavation of the ditch compared with the settlement's chronology

tuples.episode_object: the claim that the record was altered to protect an investor
tuples.time_place_scope: a venture financed by subscription with reputational exposure
tuples.mechanism: a financial motive alleged, which cannot be tested against the surviving papers
tuples.evidence_lens: the company records compared with the allegation about them

tuples.episode_object: the oral tradition of a neighbouring people about newcomers
tuples.time_place_scope: a community whose own account differs from the colonial record
tuples.mechanism: an alternative record, which was available all along and rarely consulted
tuples.evidence_lens: the recorded oral accounts compared with the colonial documents

tuples.episode_object: the artefacts of European manufacture found in later contexts
tuples.time_place_scope: sites occupied after the settlement was abandoned
tuples.mechanism: objects moving between communities, which is evidence of contact and not of fate
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavated objects compared with the trade patterns of the period

tuples.episode_object: the genetic studies proposed and their acknowledged limits
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern technique with a narrow and contested application here
tuples.mechanism: a method whose limits are the story, which is rarely how it is reported
tuples.evidence_lens: the published studies compared with the claims made about them

tuples.episode_object: the case as it is used to argue about how colonies are remembered
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern debate about which settlements are told as mysteries
tuples.mechanism: a historiographical reading, which is about attention and not evidence
tuples.evidence_lens: the modern published arguments compared with the primary record

coverage_profiles.subject: books nobody has been able to read

tuples.episode_object: an illustrated codex in an unknown script bought by a dealer
tuples.time_place_scope: a European manuscript market in the early twentieth century
tuples.mechanism: a text with no known language, which makes every reading a hypothesis
tuples.evidence_lens: the radiocarbon dating compared with the palaeographic assessments

tuples.episode_object: the plant illustrations that match no identified species
tuples.time_place_scope: a botanical tradition of copied and idealised drawings
tuples.mechanism: images that resist identification, which are read as coded, invented, or simply bad
tuples.evidence_lens: the illustrations compared with contemporary herbals of the same period

tuples.episode_object: the claim that the script encodes a known language by a cipher
tuples.time_place_scope: a century of proposed decipherments by qualified and unqualified readers
tuples.mechanism: a solution claimed repeatedly, which fails the same statistical tests each time
tuples.evidence_lens: the published proposals compared with the statistical properties of the text

tuples.episode_object: the claim that the text is an elaborate contemporary hoax
tuples.time_place_scope: an early modern market for expensive curiosities
tuples.mechanism: a hoax hypothesis, which must explain the vellum date and the internal structure
tuples.evidence_lens: the material dating compared with the hoax argument as stated

tuples.episode_object: the statistical structure that behaves like a natural language
tuples.time_place_scope: a corpus long enough for word-frequency analysis
tuples.mechanism: quantitative behaviour, which constrains the possibilities without naming one
tuples.evidence_lens: the frequency analyses compared across the studies that produced them

tuples.episode_object: the provenance chain that breaks in the seventeenth century
tuples.time_place_scope: a series of owners recorded in letters and inventories
tuples.mechanism: a gap in ownership, which is where most competing origin stories are inserted
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving letters compared with the institutional inventories

tuples.episode_object: a script found on clay tablets in a palace archive and still unread
tuples.time_place_scope: an island civilisation whose administrative records survive
tuples.mechanism: an undeciphered administrative corpus, which is dull and completely resistant
tuples.evidence_lens: the tablet corpus compared with the related script that has been read

tuples.episode_object: the related script that was deciphered and what it did not unlock
tuples.time_place_scope: two scripts sharing signs but not, apparently, a language
tuples.mechanism: a partial key that opens the wrong door, which is a specific kind of frustration
tuples.evidence_lens: the deciphered corpus compared with the undeciphered one

tuples.episode_object: an inscribed disc with stamped characters found at a single site
tuples.time_place_scope: an object unique in its technique and without a parallel
tuples.mechanism: a corpus of one, which cannot be decoded by comparison
tuples.evidence_lens: the object compared with every claimed parallel proposed for it

tuples.episode_object: the claim that the disc is a modern forgery placed in a dig
tuples.time_place_scope: an excavation whose recording practices have been questioned
tuples.mechanism: a forgery hypothesis, which the site records neither prove nor exclude
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavation notebooks compared with the forgery argument

tuples.episode_object: a river-valley script on thousands of short seal inscriptions
tuples.time_place_scope: an urban civilisation whose texts are all extremely short
tuples.mechanism: inscriptions too short for statistical attack, which may be unreadable in principle
tuples.evidence_lens: the sign corpus compared with the length distribution of the inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: the argument that the marks are not writing at all
tuples.time_place_scope: a scholarly dispute about what counts as a script
tuples.mechanism: a definitional dispute, which changes the question rather than answering it
tuples.evidence_lens: the published arguments compared with the sign frequencies they cite

tuples.episode_object: a coded diary kept by a private person for decades
tuples.time_place_scope: a household archive with a personal shorthand
tuples.mechanism: a private system with no key, which is usually solvable and sometimes is not
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving volumes compared with the family papers around them

tuples.episode_object: a nineteenth-century book printed in an invented alphabet
tuples.time_place_scope: a period of constructed languages and private printing
tuples.mechanism: a deliberate invention, which is a solved kind of mystery with an unfound key
tuples.evidence_lens: the printing records compared with the author's other publications

tuples.episode_object: the machine-learning attempts and what they actually produced
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern period applying statistical models to old corpora
tuples.mechanism: a technique producing plausible output, which is not the same as a reading
tuples.evidence_lens: the published model outputs compared with the standards for a decipherment

tuples.episode_object: the standard a decipherment has to meet to be accepted
tuples.time_place_scope: a discipline with an explicit and demanding bar
tuples.mechanism: an agreed test, which is why almost every announced solution fails
tuples.evidence_lens: the accepted decipherments compared with the criteria they satisfied

tuples.episode_object: the marginal notes added by a later owner in a known hand
tuples.time_place_scope: a manuscript annotated by someone who also could not read it
tuples.mechanism: a reader's failure recorded in the margin, which is evidence about reception
tuples.evidence_lens: the marginalia compared with the owner's identified handwriting

tuples.episode_object: the missing quires and where they can be shown to have been
tuples.time_place_scope: a codex whose collation reveals absent leaves
tuples.mechanism: physical absence established by binding, which shows the text is incomplete
tuples.evidence_lens: the collation analysis compared with the surviving page sequence

tuples.episode_object: the multispectral imaging that recovered erased text elsewhere
tuples.time_place_scope: a technique with real successes on other manuscripts
tuples.mechanism: a method that works and has not worked here, which is informative in itself
tuples.evidence_lens: the imaging results compared with the successes on comparable objects

tuples.episode_object: the case as an example of how a null result gets reported
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern media environment that reports attempts as breakthroughs
tuples.mechanism: a pattern in the reporting, which is about journalism and not the manuscript
tuples.evidence_lens: the published papers compared with the coverage they received

coverage_profiles.subject: messages that were never decoded

tuples.episode_object: a set of ciphered notes said to locate a buried cache
tuples.time_place_scope: a nineteenth-century pamphlet describing three coded papers
tuples.mechanism: a cipher whose key is a published document, which was found for one paper only
tuples.evidence_lens: the pamphlet compared with the key text that solved the second paper

tuples.episode_object: the second paper, solved with a founding document as its key
tuples.time_place_scope: a cipher using a numbered word list from a well-known text
tuples.mechanism: a solved example proving the method, which makes the unsolved ones harder to dismiss
tuples.evidence_lens: the solved plaintext compared with the key text used to produce it

tuples.episode_object: the argument that the whole set is a nineteenth-century invention
tuples.time_place_scope: a period of treasure pamphlets sold for a profit
tuples.mechanism: a fabrication hypothesis, which fits the commercial context and not every detail
tuples.evidence_lens: the pamphlet's publishing record compared with the ciphers' internal statistics

tuples.episode_object: the statistical tests that suggest one paper is not a real cipher
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern analysis of the number sequences
tuples.mechanism: a test suggesting nonsense, which is contested and not conclusive
tuples.evidence_lens: the published analyses compared with each other

tuples.episode_object: a wartime message found attached to the remains of a carrier pigeon
tuples.time_place_scope: a period of routine encrypted messages sent by bird
tuples.mechanism: a short message with a one-time key, which may be undecipherable in principle
tuples.evidence_lens: the recovered message compared with the surviving code-book records

tuples.episode_object: a message sent in a code whose books were destroyed by policy
tuples.time_place_scope: a service that routinely destroyed superseded key material
tuples.mechanism: a key destroyed deliberately, which makes the silence procedural rather than sinister
tuples.evidence_lens: the destruction schedules compared with the message's date

tuples.episode_object: an inscription on a sculpture with several sections still unread
tuples.time_place_scope: an artwork installed with a deliberate puzzle in it
tuples.mechanism: a puzzle made on purpose, which has a solution and an author who knows it
tuples.evidence_lens: the published solved sections compared with the artist's own statements

tuples.episode_object: the transcription errors that circulated for years
tuples.time_place_scope: a puzzle copied by hand and republished repeatedly
tuples.mechanism: an error in the copy, which wastes decades of work on a wrong text
tuples.evidence_lens: the corrected transcription compared with the versions in circulation

tuples.episode_object: a series of coded advertisements placed in a newspaper
tuples.time_place_scope: a period when personal columns carried private messages
tuples.mechanism: a private correspondence in public, which is solvable and mostly banal
tuples.evidence_lens: the newspaper archive compared with the solutions published later

tuples.episode_object: a gravestone inscription of letters with no obvious reading
tuples.time_place_scope: a churchyard monument with an unexplained sequence
tuples.mechanism: a short text with no context, which cannot be attacked statistically
tuples.evidence_lens: the monument compared with the parish records of the person buried

tuples.episode_object: a manuscript cipher used by a diplomatic service and later broken
tuples.time_place_scope: an early modern state with a professional cipher office
tuples.mechanism: a system broken by its own users' errors, which is the usual way
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving despatches compared with the code-breakers' working papers

tuples.episode_object: the claim that a literary work contains a hidden authorial signature
tuples.time_place_scope: a long-running dispute about the authorship of a body of plays
tuples.mechanism: a claimed cipher in a text, which fails when the same method is tested elsewhere
tuples.evidence_lens: the claimed method compared with the results it gives on control texts

tuples.episode_object: a set of postcards written in a private shorthand between two people
tuples.time_place_scope: a correspondence intended to be private and never meant to survive
tuples.mechanism: a personal system, which is solvable and raises a question about whether it should be
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving cards compared with the shorthand systems of the period

tuples.episode_object: a number station broadcast recorded and catalogued by listeners
tuples.time_place_scope: a shortwave band monitored by hobbyists for decades
tuples.mechanism: an unattributed transmission, which is documented in detail and explained by nobody
tuples.evidence_lens: the listener recordings compared with the transmitter locations identified

tuples.episode_object: the acknowledgement by a state that such broadcasts existed
tuples.time_place_scope: a period when an old practice was confirmed after the fact
tuples.mechanism: a partial official confirmation, which answers what and not which
tuples.evidence_lens: the official statements compared with the catalogue of recorded broadcasts

tuples.episode_object: a coded notebook found in a hotel room with an unidentified man
tuples.time_place_scope: an investigation with an unnamed subject and a short document
tuples.mechanism: two mysteries reinforcing each other, which is why the case is remembered
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquest record compared with the notebook as photographed

tuples.episode_object: the strip of paper found sewn into a pocket
tuples.time_place_scope: an object recovered during a post-mortem examination
tuples.mechanism: a physical concealment, which proves intent without revealing content
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquest exhibits compared with the later analyses of them

tuples.episode_object: the claim that a message is a running key from a lost book
tuples.time_place_scope: a cipher type that cannot be broken without the source text
tuples.mechanism: a hypothesis that is unfalsifiable by construction, which ends the analysis
tuples.evidence_lens: the cipher type's known properties compared with the claim made

tuples.episode_object: the community of amateur solvers and what they have contributed
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern distributed effort organised online
tuples.mechanism: distributed attention producing real corrections, which is a genuine result
tuples.evidence_lens: the community's published corrections compared with the official record

tuples.episode_object: the case as an argument about when to stop working on a cipher
tuples.time_place_scope: a discipline with limited attention and many candidates
tuples.mechanism: a question about resource allocation, which is the least romantic part of the field
tuples.evidence_lens: the published assessments compared with the effort actually spent

coverage_profiles.subject: the dead who were never identified

tuples.episode_object: a well-dressed man found on a beach with no name in his clothes
tuples.time_place_scope: a coastal city in the years after a war
tuples.mechanism: a body with every label removed, which makes concealment the first established fact
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquest record compared with the police file as later released

tuples.episode_object: the scrap of printed paper found in a hidden pocket
tuples.time_place_scope: a garment with a concealed compartment sewn into it
tuples.mechanism: a deliberate concealment, which proves intent and identifies nothing
tuples.evidence_lens: the recovered scrap compared with the book it was torn from

tuples.episode_object: the book from which the scrap was torn, found in a parked car
tuples.time_place_scope: a vehicle left unlocked in the same city
tuples.mechanism: an object arriving by an unexplained route, which extends the case without solving it
tuples.evidence_lens: the recovered book compared with the scrap and the marks written in it

tuples.episode_object: the dental and post-mortem records and what they excluded
tuples.time_place_scope: an examination performed to a standard of its time
tuples.mechanism: an examination that rules candidates out, which narrows without naming
tuples.evidence_lens: the post-mortem report compared with the missing-person records checked

tuples.episode_object: the plaster bust made from the body before burial
tuples.time_place_scope: a preservation measure taken with identification in mind
tuples.mechanism: an object made for a future technique, which was foresighted and still insufficient
tuples.evidence_lens: the bust compared with the later reconstructions made from it

tuples.episode_object: the exhumation and the modern analysis of the remains
tuples.time_place_scope: a later period with techniques the original examiners lacked
tuples.mechanism: a technique applied decades later, which produced a partial result
tuples.evidence_lens: the modern analysis compared with the original post-mortem findings

tuples.episode_object: a body found in a wood with a wedding ring and nothing else
tuples.time_place_scope: a rural district with a small and complete set of records
tuples.mechanism: a case in a small population, which should be solvable and is not
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquest record compared with the parish and county records

tuples.episode_object: a woman found in a river with a laundry mark on her clothing
tuples.time_place_scope: a period when commercial laundries marked garments individually
tuples.mechanism: an identifier that should have worked, which failed because a business closed
tuples.evidence_lens: the laundry mark compared with the trade registers of the period

tuples.episode_object: the claim that the case was a foreign intelligence matter
tuples.time_place_scope: a period of active espionage in the same city
tuples.mechanism: an intelligence hypothesis, which is unsupported by any released file
tuples.evidence_lens: the released intelligence holdings compared with the claim as stated

tuples.episode_object: the missing-person report that was withdrawn and never revisited
tuples.time_place_scope: a family that stopped looking for reasons of its own
tuples.mechanism: a withdrawn report, which removes a candidate from the record permanently
tuples.evidence_lens: the withdrawn report compared with the identification attempts made

tuples.episode_object: a burial in an unmarked grave paid for by a parish
tuples.time_place_scope: a locality obliged to bury an unidentified person
tuples.mechanism: a public burial creating a permanent record, which is how such cases survive
tuples.evidence_lens: the burial register compared with the coroner's disposal order

tuples.episode_object: the facial reconstruction that produced two very different faces
tuples.time_place_scope: a technique applied twice by different practitioners
tuples.mechanism: two reconstructions disagreeing, which shows the method's real uncertainty
tuples.evidence_lens: the two reconstructions compared with the skull measurements

tuples.episode_object: the fingerprints taken and checked against no matching set
tuples.time_place_scope: a period with an incomplete national fingerprint collection
tuples.mechanism: a check against a partial database, which is a null result and not an exclusion
tuples.evidence_lens: the fingerprint record compared with the collection's coverage at the time

tuples.episode_object: the clothing labels traced to a single manufacturer and no further
tuples.time_place_scope: a garment trade with wide distribution and no sales records
tuples.mechanism: a trace that ends at a factory, which narrows nothing useful
tuples.evidence_lens: the manufacturer's records compared with the distribution of the garment

tuples.episode_object: the isotope analysis suggesting a childhood spent elsewhere
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern technique giving a region rather than a place
tuples.mechanism: a geographic indication, which reduces the search area and not the candidates
tuples.evidence_lens: the isotope results compared with the migration records of the period

tuples.episode_object: the case file that was destroyed under a retention schedule
tuples.time_place_scope: an archive with a routine disposal policy
tuples.mechanism: records destroyed by policy, which looks like concealment and is not
tuples.evidence_lens: the retention schedule compared with the file's absence

tuples.episode_object: the newspaper campaign that produced two hundred false leads

tuples.episode_object: the standard now used for what an instrument case must include

tuples.episode_object: a signal detected during a search programme and traced to a satellite

tuples.episode_object: the signal that was announced and retracted within a week

tuples.episode_object: the interviewer who spoke to the witnesses within days
tuples.time_place_scope: an investigation begun quickly enough to matter

tuples.episode_object: the drawings the witnesses made before discussing it
tuples.time_place_scope: a procedure designed to prevent contamination between witnesses
tuples.mechanism: an anti-contamination method, which is rarely used and hugely informative

tuples.episode_object: a religious apparition reported by a crowd at an announced time

tuples.episode_object: the meteorological explanation offered for that event

tuples.time_place_scope: an occasion with a large expectant crowd

tuples.evidence_lens: the launch record compared with the sighting times and bearings

tuples.time_place_scope: a modern approach treating the crowd as the subject

tuples.evidence_lens: the mass sighting cases compared for their common structure

tuples.episode_object: the facial recognition trial disclosed by a freedom of information request

tuples.mechanism: a trial revealed by request, which is how most such programmes become public
tuples.evidence_lens: the disclosed documents compared with the force's public statements

tuples.episode_object: the audit that found a system had never been evaluated for accuracy
tuples.time_place_scope: an oversight body examining a deployed technology
tuples.mechanism: a deployed system without an evaluation, which is a governance failure not a plot
tuples.evidence_lens: the audit report compared with the procurement justification

tuples.episode_object: the register of interception warrants and what it does not record
tuples.time_place_scope: a statutory register with defined and limited contents
tuples.mechanism: a record designed to reassure, which omits the interesting categories
tuples.evidence_lens: the register's contents compared with the categories it excludes

tuples.episode_object: the informant programme disclosed by a public inquiry
tuples.time_place_scope: an inquiry into undercover policing over several decades
tuples.mechanism: an inquiry with statutory powers, which extracts documents nothing else could
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquiry evidence compared with the organisations' own records

tuples.episode_object: the destroyed records that the inquiry could not recover
tuples.time_place_scope: a set of files disposed of before the inquiry was established
tuples.mechanism: destruction before an inquiry, which is documented and unprovable as to intent
tuples.evidence_lens: the disposal records compared with the inquiry's requests

tuples.episode_object: the whistle-blower protections that did and did not apply
tuples.time_place_scope: a legal framework with narrow categories
tuples.mechanism: a protection regime that excludes the cases it is invoked for, which is a design question
tuples.evidence_lens: the statutory protections compared with the cases that tested them

tuples.episode_object: the international agreements that governed sharing between services
tuples.time_place_scope: arrangements between allied states over many decades
tuples.mechanism: a sharing arrangement, which allows domestic limits to be circumvented lawfully
tuples.evidence_lens: the released agreements compared with the domestic legal limits

tuples.episode_object: the distinction between what was secret and what was merely unexamined
tuples.time_place_scope: a subject where inattention explains more than concealment
tuples.mechanism: inattention rather than concealment, which is the boring and usual answer
tuples.evidence_lens: the disclosed records compared with the public discussion before disclosure

tuples.episode_object: the case as a history of how oversight is created after the fact
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern reading of fifty years of inquiry and statute
tuples.mechanism: a documented cycle of scandal and rule, which is the durable finding
tuples.evidence_lens: the successive inquiries compared with the statutes that followed each

coverage_profiles.subject: documents released with the important parts blacked out

tuples.episode_object: a file released with the substantive paragraphs removed
tuples.time_place_scope: an access request answered with a heavily marked document
tuples.mechanism: a release that is technically compliant and substantively empty, which is a real pattern
tuples.evidence_lens: the redacted release compared with the exemptions cited for each removal

tuples.episode_object: the exemption codes printed in the margins and what they mean
tuples.time_place_scope: a statutory scheme with numbered grounds for withholding
tuples.mechanism: a legal vocabulary in the margin, which tells a reader exactly what is being claimed
tuples.evidence_lens: the cited exemptions compared with the statute's definitions

tuples.episode_object: the appeal that produced a less redacted version of the same file
tuples.time_place_scope: an internal review conducted after a challenge
tuples.mechanism: a second release with less removed, which shows the first was over-applied
tuples.evidence_lens: the two releases compared line by line

tuples.episode_object: the tribunal that ordered disclosure over the agency's objection
tuples.time_place_scope: an independent body reviewing a refusal
tuples.mechanism: an external review, which is the only reliable check on over-redaction
tuples.evidence_lens: the tribunal's decision compared with the agency's stated grounds

tuples.episode_object: the document released in full in one country and redacted in another
tuples.time_place_scope: a shared record held by two allied administrations
tuples.mechanism: an inconsistency between jurisdictions, which reveals the withheld content
tuples.evidence_lens: the two national releases of the same document compared

tuples.episode_object: the redaction that failed because the text was still selectable
tuples.time_place_scope: a digital release where the marking was cosmetic
tuples.mechanism: a technical failure, which discloses the content and embarrasses everyone
tuples.evidence_lens: the released file compared with the extracted underlying text

tuples.episode_object: the names removed to protect people who had already died
tuples.time_place_scope: a release applying personal exemptions mechanically
tuples.mechanism: an exemption applied without checking, which is bureaucratic rather than sinister
tuples.evidence_lens: the redacted names compared with the public death records

tuples.episode_object: the release that redacted material already published elsewhere
tuples.time_place_scope: a file whose contents were in a library the whole time
tuples.mechanism: a redaction of public material, which shows the process is not content-aware
tuples.evidence_lens: the redacted passages compared with the published sources

tuples.episode_object: the reading room where a file may be seen but not copied
tuples.time_place_scope: an archive offering supervised access without reproduction
tuples.mechanism: access without a copy, which limits scrutiny without refusing it
tuples.evidence_lens: the reading room conditions compared with the standard access rules

tuples.episode_object: the file whose existence is neither confirmed nor denied
tuples.time_place_scope: a response refusing to say whether records exist
tuples.mechanism: a refusal to confirm existence, which is lawful and maximally frustrating
tuples.evidence_lens: the response compared with the statutory basis for the position

tuples.episode_object: the historian who reconstructed a redacted passage from context
tuples.time_place_scope: a scholar working from surrounding documents
tuples.mechanism: reconstruction from context, which sometimes recovers the substance entirely
tuples.evidence_lens: the reconstruction compared with the later unredacted release

tuples.episode_object: the automatic declassification deadline and the exemptions from it
tuples.time_place_scope: a system with a default period and a review process
tuples.mechanism: a default with wide exemptions, which determines what actually becomes public
tuples.evidence_lens: the declassification statistics compared with the exemption rates

tuples.episode_object: the review that reclassified documents already in public reading rooms
tuples.time_place_scope: a programme withdrawing records that had been released
tuples.mechanism: a reclassification of public material, which is unusual and was itself disclosed
tuples.evidence_lens: the withdrawal lists compared with the reading room records

tuples.episode_object: the volume of material and the staffing available to review it
tuples.time_place_scope: an archive with more records than reviewers
tuples.mechanism: a resource constraint, which explains most delay better than any intention
tuples.evidence_lens: the review backlog compared with the staffing levels

tuples.episode_object: the request that was answered eleven years after it was made
tuples.time_place_scope: an access system with no effective time limit in practice
tuples.mechanism: delay functioning as refusal, which is a structural rather than a decided outcome
tuples.evidence_lens: the request date compared with the response date

tuples.episode_object: the fee regime that made a large request impractical
tuples.time_place_scope: a scheme charging for search and copying
tuples.mechanism: cost as a barrier, which shapes what is asked for
tuples.evidence_lens: the fee schedule compared with the requests actually pursued

tuples.episode_object: the leaked version that circulated before the official release
tuples.time_place_scope: a document available unofficially years earlier
tuples.mechanism: an unofficial version, which is unverifiable and usually accurate
tuples.evidence_lens: the leaked text compared with the official release when it came

tuples.episode_object: the index that survived even though the files did not
tuples.time_place_scope: a finding aid outliving the material it describes
tuples.mechanism: a catalogue of absent records, which proves what existed
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving index compared with the holdings actually retained

tuples.episode_object: the personal papers deposited by an official after retirement
tuples.time_place_scope: a private deposit containing official material
tuples.mechanism: official records in a private archive, which is irregular and often the only copy
tuples.evidence_lens: the deposited papers compared with the official file

tuples.episode_object: the case as an argument about what redaction actually protects
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern debate about the balance struck in practice
tuples.mechanism: an argument about proportion, which is the real question under every case
tuples.evidence_lens: the released material compared with the harms the exemptions describe

coverage_profiles.subject: archives that were sealed for a stated number of years

tuples.episode_object: a state archive closed for a century by an explicit instruction
tuples.time_place_scope: a collection deposited with a specified opening date
tuples.mechanism: a closure with a date, which converts secrecy into waiting
tuples.evidence_lens: the deposit instrument compared with the archive's published access schedule

tuples.episode_object: the papers of an inquiry sealed to protect witnesses
tuples.time_place_scope: an investigation that took evidence under a guarantee
tuples.mechanism: a closure protecting people, which is defensible and indistinguishable from concealment
tuples.evidence_lens: the sealing order compared with the inquiry's published findings

tuples.episode_object: the medical records closed for the lifetime of the individuals
tuples.time_place_scope: an archive applying a personal confidentiality period
tuples.mechanism: a closure keyed to lives, which opens gradually and unpredictably
tuples.evidence_lens: the access policy compared with the records' subject dates

tuples.episode_object: the file that was opened on schedule and contained almost nothing
tuples.time_place_scope: an eagerly awaited release with a disappointing content
tuples.mechanism: an anticlimax, which is the commonest outcome of a scheduled opening
tuples.evidence_lens: the released contents compared with the expectations published beforehand

tuples.episode_object: the file that was extended for a further period without explanation
tuples.time_place_scope: a closure renewed as its expiry approached
tuples.mechanism: an extension without stated grounds, which converts patience into suspicion
tuples.evidence_lens: the extension notice compared with the original closure terms

tuples.episode_object: the royal or head-of-state papers held under separate arrangements
tuples.time_place_scope: a collection outside the ordinary public records regime
tuples.mechanism: a separate regime, which places a body of material beyond normal access
tuples.evidence_lens: the governing arrangements compared with the general public records law

tuples.episode_object: the church archive with its own access rules and its own history
tuples.time_place_scope: a religious institution holding records of long historical interest
tuples.mechanism: an institutional archive with its own rules, which opens on its own terms
tuples.evidence_lens: the institution's access policy compared with the material it holds

tuples.episode_object: the release of a papal or ecclesiastical period file
tuples.time_place_scope: an archive opening a defined pontificate to researchers
tuples.mechanism: a scheduled institutional opening, which produces genuine historical revision
tuples.evidence_lens: the released material compared with the historiography that preceded it

tuples.episode_object: the corporate archive sealed under a legal settlement
tuples.time_place_scope: a company that agreed to confidentiality as part of a resolution
tuples.mechanism: contractual secrecy, which is enforceable and outlives everyone involved
tuples.evidence_lens: the settlement terms compared with the material they cover

tuples.episode_object: the university collection restricted by a donor's condition
tuples.time_place_scope: a private deposit with strings attached
tuples.mechanism: donor control, which places a condition on public scholarship
tuples.evidence_lens: the deposit agreement compared with the institution's access policy

tuples.episode_object: the archive whose catalogue is public and whose contents are not
tuples.time_place_scope: a collection where researchers know exactly what they cannot see
tuples.mechanism: visible absence, which is more useful than an unlisted holding
tuples.evidence_lens: the published catalogue compared with the access restrictions

tuples.episode_object: the estate papers released only after the last surviving child died
tuples.time_place_scope: a family archive with an access condition tied to lives
tuples.mechanism: a family condition, which delays scholarship by a generation or two
tuples.evidence_lens: the deposit conditions compared with the family's own dates

tuples.episode_object: the file that was destroyed rather than sealed
tuples.time_place_scope: an office choosing disposal over closure
tuples.mechanism: destruction as an alternative to closure, which is permanent and cheaper
tuples.evidence_lens: the disposal schedule compared with the retention policy

tuples.episode_object: the archive damaged by fire before the opening date
tuples.time_place_scope: a repository that lost material to an accident
tuples.mechanism: material lost to accident, which is indistinguishable from concealment to a suspicious reader
tuples.evidence_lens: the damage report compared with the catalogue of what was held

tuples.episode_object: the copy that turned out to exist in a second archive
tuples.time_place_scope: a duplicate held by another institution
tuples.mechanism: a duplicate defeating a closure, which is how many sealed matters become known
tuples.evidence_lens: the two institutions' holdings compared

tuples.episode_object: the researcher granted privileged access and the questions that raised
tuples.time_place_scope: a scholar admitted to a closed collection before general opening
tuples.mechanism: privileged access, which produces scholarship and a legitimate complaint
tuples.evidence_lens: the resulting publication compared with the access conditions granted

tuples.episode_object: the summary published in place of the records themselves
tuples.time_place_scope: an institution releasing a description rather than documents
tuples.mechanism: a summary substituted for evidence, which cannot be checked
tuples.evidence_lens: the published summary compared with the material it describes

tuples.episode_object: the material released early because of a public inquiry's demand
tuples.time_place_scope: an inquiry with power to compel production
tuples.mechanism: compulsion overriding a closure, which is the most effective route
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquiry's production orders compared with the archive's access rules

tuples.episode_object: the opening that changed a settled historical account
tuples.time_place_scope: a release that overturned a widely held view
tuples.mechanism: a genuine revision on opening, which is uncommon and worth recording when it happens
tuples.evidence_lens: the released material compared with the historiography before it

tuples.episode_object: the case for judging a closure by its stated reason
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern approach that reads the instrument rather than the rumour
tuples.mechanism: reading the closure terms, which is unglamorous and answers most questions
tuples.evidence_lens: the closure instruments compared with the claims made about them

coverage_profiles.subject: records that were destroyed

tuples.episode_object: a service archive burned in a records centre fire
tuples.time_place_scope: a repository holding the only copies of millions of personnel files
tuples.mechanism: an accidental loss on a vast scale, which is routinely described as suspicious
tuples.evidence_lens: the fire investigation report compared with the holdings inventory

tuples.episode_object: the reconstruction effort that rebuilt files from other sources
tuples.time_place_scope: an archive assembling substitutes from payroll and medical records
tuples.mechanism: a reconstruction from fragments, which is partial and genuinely impressive
tuples.evidence_lens: the reconstructed files compared with the categories of the originals

tuples.episode_object: a ministry's papers pulped as part of a routine review
tuples.time_place_scope: a records office applying a disposal schedule
tuples.mechanism: routine destruction, which removes material nobody thought would matter
tuples.evidence_lens: the disposal schedule compared with the historical questions later asked

tuples.episode_object: the colonial records removed rather than handed over at independence
tuples.time_place_scope: a transfer of power with a documented removal operation
tuples.mechanism: a deliberate removal, which was itself documented and later admitted
tuples.evidence_lens: the transfer records compared with the archives eventually disclosed

tuples.episode_object: the migrated archive whose existence was denied in litigation
tuples.time_place_scope: a legal case where the government's own holdings were at issue
tuples.mechanism: a denial contradicted by discovery, which produced a formal acknowledgement
tuples.evidence_lens: the court filings compared with the archive as subsequently released

tuples.episode_object: the papers destroyed by a family before a house was sold
tuples.time_place_scope: a private archive dispersed with no record
tuples.mechanism: private destruction, which is nobody's fault and permanently closes questions
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving correspondence compared with the references to lost papers

tuples.episode_object: the digital records lost when a system was decommissioned
tuples.time_place_scope: an organisation that migrated without preserving the old format
tuples.mechanism: loss by obsolescence, which is the modern form of destruction
tuples.evidence_lens: the migration records compared with the retention requirements

tuples.episode_object: the emails deleted under a retention policy during an investigation
tuples.time_place_scope: an organisation with an automatic deletion period
tuples.mechanism: automatic deletion during scrutiny, which is lawful and looks deliberate
tuples.evidence_lens: the retention policy compared with the investigation's timeline

tuples.episode_object: the shredding contract that ran for weeks before an inspection
tuples.time_place_scope: an office disposing of material ahead of an announced visit
tuples.mechanism: timing that invites inference, which is rarely provable either way
tuples.evidence_lens: the contractor's records compared with the inspection schedule

tuples.episode_object: the archive lost in wartime bombing and the copies that survived abroad
tuples.time_place_scope: a repository destroyed with duplicates in another country
tuples.mechanism: survival by duplication, which is the only defence against destruction
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving foreign copies compared with the destroyed originals' catalogue

tuples.episode_object: the register that recorded what was destroyed and when
tuples.time_place_scope: an office that documented its own disposals
tuples.mechanism: a destruction register, which is the most useful record an archive can keep
tuples.evidence_lens: the destruction register compared with the missing series

tuples.episode_object: the file that was never created because a decision was taken orally
tuples.time_place_scope: an organisation with a culture of unminuted meetings
tuples.mechanism: an absence by practice, which cannot be recovered by any technique
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving diaries compared with the absence of minutes

tuples.episode_object: the minutes that were written to be read later by outsiders
tuples.time_place_scope: a body aware that its record would be published
tuples.mechanism: a record written for an audience, which is evidence about intent and not events
tuples.evidence_lens: the minutes compared with the participants' contemporaneous notes

tuples.episode_object: the records held by a contractor and destroyed at contract end
tuples.time_place_scope: a service delivered privately with records held outside the public regime
tuples.mechanism: outsourcing removing records from a preservation regime, which is a structural gap
tuples.evidence_lens: the contract terms compared with the public records requirements

tuples.episode_object: the police file destroyed after a fixed period and the case still open
tuples.time_place_scope: a force applying a retention rule to an unresolved matter
tuples.mechanism: a rule applied without a case-by-case check, which loses solvable cases
tuples.evidence_lens: the retention policy compared with the case's open status

tuples.episode_object: the evidence exhibits disposed of before a technique existed to test them
tuples.time_place_scope: an evidence store clearing space by policy
tuples.mechanism: material destroyed before it could be useful, which is the commonest tragedy here
tuples.evidence_lens: the disposal records compared with the dates the technique became available

tuples.episode_object: the microfilm made before destruction and later found unreadable
tuples.time_place_scope: a preservation copy on a degraded medium
tuples.mechanism: a preservation failure, which is worse than no copy because it prevented one
tuples.evidence_lens: the microfilm condition report compared with the destruction authorisation

tuples.episode_object: the inquiry that could not proceed because the material was gone
tuples.time_place_scope: an investigation defeated by an empty archive
tuples.mechanism: an inquiry unable to reach a finding, which is honest and unsatisfying
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquiry's statement compared with the records it sought

tuples.episode_object: the legislation that made destruction an offence during an investigation
tuples.time_place_scope: a statutory response to a documented case
tuples.mechanism: a rule created by a scandal, which is the usual origin of records law
tuples.evidence_lens: the statute compared with the case that prompted it

tuples.episode_object: the case for treating an absent record as an absence and not a proof
tuples.time_place_scope: a methodological point that applies to every case in this collection
tuples.mechanism: an epistemic rule, which is the single most useful thing to state plainly
tuples.evidence_lens: the documented destructions compared with the inferences drawn from them

coverage_profiles.subject: official statements that were later reversed

tuples.episode_object: a press release issued and withdrawn within twenty-four hours
tuples.time_place_scope: a public information office correcting itself in public
tuples.mechanism: a reversal on the record, which becomes the foundation of everything afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the two statements compared with the internal correspondence between them

tuples.episode_object: a denial of a programme's existence given before a legislature
tuples.time_place_scope: sworn testimony contradicted by a later release
tuples.mechanism: testimony contradicted by documents, which is the most consequential kind of reversal
tuples.evidence_lens: the transcript compared with the documents released afterwards

tuples.episode_object: a maritime incident described one way and revised after an inquiry
tuples.time_place_scope: an event whose first account came from one side only
tuples.mechanism: a first account revised by evidence, which is how inquiry is supposed to work
tuples.evidence_lens: the initial statement compared with the inquiry's findings

tuples.episode_object: a cause of death given at the time and changed at a fresh inquest
tuples.time_place_scope: a legal process reopened on new evidence
tuples.mechanism: a formal legal revision, which is rare and completely authoritative
tuples.evidence_lens: the two inquest findings compared with the evidence heard at each

tuples.episode_object: a safety assurance given about a material later withdrawn
tuples.time_place_scope: a regulatory position reversed as evidence accumulated
tuples.mechanism: a reversal driven by science, which is correct and reads as prior deception
tuples.evidence_lens: the successive regulatory positions compared with the evidence available at each

tuples.episode_object: a statement that no records existed, followed by their production
tuples.time_place_scope: an access request answered wrongly and corrected on appeal
tuples.mechanism: an erroneous nil return, which is usually incompetence and never reads that way
tuples.evidence_lens: the original response compared with the records eventually produced

tuples.episode_object: an official denial maintained while a court order required disclosure
tuples.time_place_scope: a case where two obligations conflicted
tuples.mechanism: a conflict of duties, which produces statements that are true and misleading
tuples.evidence_lens: the court order compared with the public statements made

tuples.episode_object: a casualty figure revised upward over several years
tuples.time_place_scope: an event whose toll was counted repeatedly
tuples.mechanism: a figure that grew with counting, which is normal and widely misread
tuples.evidence_lens: the successive official figures compared with the counting methodology

tuples.episode_object: an assurance about a site's contamination reversed after monitoring
tuples.time_place_scope: a location declared safe and later restricted
tuples.mechanism: a reversal on measurement, which is the system working slowly
tuples.evidence_lens: the monitoring data compared with the successive official positions

tuples.episode_object: a claim about the cause of an accident revised by a technical report
tuples.time_place_scope: an investigation whose preliminary view did not survive analysis
tuples.mechanism: a preliminary view corrected, which is standard practice and always reported as scandal
tuples.evidence_lens: the preliminary statement compared with the final technical report

tuples.episode_object: a denial of a meeting that a diary later showed had happened
tuples.time_place_scope: a record surviving in a private appointment book
tuples.mechanism: a small document defeating a large denial, which is a recurring pattern
tuples.evidence_lens: the diary entry compared with the public denial

tuples.episode_object: an official history published and then quietly corrected
tuples.time_place_scope: a commissioned account revised in a later edition
tuples.mechanism: a correction made without announcement, which is honest and invisible
tuples.evidence_lens: the two editions compared page by page

tuples.episode_object: a public statement drafted by a body with an interest in the outcome
tuples.time_place_scope: an announcement written by the organisation being examined
tuples.mechanism: self-description as evidence, which is weak and constantly relied upon
tuples.evidence_lens: the statement compared with the underlying documents

tuples.episode_object: a categorical denial replaced by a carefully limited one
tuples.time_place_scope: a shift in wording between two statements weeks apart
tuples.mechanism: a narrowing of language, which signals more than the content does
tuples.evidence_lens: the two statements compared word by word

tuples.episode_object: an apology issued decades after the original denial
tuples.time_place_scope: a formal acknowledgement long after the participants had gone
tuples.mechanism: an apology as a documentary act, which closes a record and not a wound
tuples.evidence_lens: the apology compared with the denials it supersedes

tuples.episode_object: the inquiry that found no bad faith and a great deal of error
tuples.time_place_scope: an investigation distinguishing incompetence from concealment
tuples.mechanism: a finding of error rather than intent, which nobody believes and is usually right
tuples.evidence_lens: the inquiry's reasoning compared with the evidence it heard

tuples.episode_object: the official who corrected the record after leaving office
tuples.time_place_scope: a former post-holder speaking without constraint
tuples.mechanism: a correction from outside, which is credible and unverifiable in equal measure
tuples.evidence_lens: the later statement compared with the record made while in office

tuples.episode_object: the reversal that came about because a foreign archive opened
tuples.time_place_scope: a case resolved by another state's records
tuples.mechanism: an external archive settling a domestic question, which is common and underused
tuples.evidence_lens: the foreign records compared with the domestic public statements

tuples.episode_object: the persistence of the original statement in every retelling
tuples.time_place_scope: a case where the corrected version never displaced the first
tuples.mechanism: a correction that fails to circulate, which is the general fate of corrections
tuples.evidence_lens: the corrected record compared with the popular accounts still in print

tuples.episode_object: the case as an argument for reading a first statement as provisional
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern approach to official communication
tuples.mechanism: a rule for reading, which is the practical lesson from all of these
tuples.evidence_lens: the first statements compared with the final findings across many cases

coverage_profiles.subject: money that went missing

tuples.episode_object: a very large sum of cash lost from a secure store during a transfer
tuples.time_place_scope: a currency movement with documented weights and counts
tuples.mechanism: a loss inside a documented process, which narrows the possibilities sharply
tuples.evidence_lens: the transfer records compared with the audit findings

tuples.episode_object: the audit that could not reconcile a department's accounts
tuples.time_place_scope: a public body with an unqualified sum unaccounted for
tuples.mechanism: an accounting gap, which is almost never theft and always reported as such
tuples.evidence_lens: the audit report compared with the accounting system's own limitations

tuples.episode_object: the difference between money unaccounted for and money missing
tuples.time_place_scope: a technical distinction that most reporting ignores
tuples.mechanism: a vocabulary problem, which produces most of the alarm in these stories
tuples.evidence_lens: the audit terminology compared with the coverage it received

tuples.episode_object: a payroll fraud that ran for years inside an organisation
tuples.time_place_scope: an institution with weak separation of duties
tuples.mechanism: a control failure, which is the mechanism in nearly every case
tuples.evidence_lens: the internal audit findings compared with the control framework on paper

tuples.episode_object: the funds transferred out of a central bank account by instruction
tuples.time_place_scope: a case involving fraudulent payment messages
tuples.mechanism: an instruction that looked genuine, which is the whole of modern financial crime
tuples.evidence_lens: the payment records compared with the authentication procedures in force

tuples.episode_object: the portion of the money that was recovered and the portion that was not
tuples.time_place_scope: a case with partial recovery through international cooperation
tuples.mechanism: partial recovery, which is the realistic outcome and rarely reported
tuples.evidence_lens: the recovery records compared with the original loss

tuples.episode_object: a treasury shipment lost during the collapse of a government
tuples.time_place_scope: a period of disorder with incomplete records
tuples.mechanism: a loss during a collapse, which cannot be investigated because the records went too
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving inventories compared with the receiving state's records

tuples.episode_object: the claim of a hoard hidden by a retreating administration
tuples.time_place_scope: a period producing many such claims and few recoveries
tuples.mechanism: a persistent hoard claim, which survives every failed search
tuples.evidence_lens: the search records compared with the claims as published

tuples.episode_object: the gold reserves moved abroad and accounted for decades later
tuples.time_place_scope: a wartime transfer with a paper trail on both ends
tuples.mechanism: a documented movement, which resolves a rumour completely
tuples.evidence_lens: the shipping records compared with the receiving institution's ledgers

tuples.episode_object: the charity whose funds were traced to unrelated accounts
tuples.time_place_scope: an organisation examined by a regulator
tuples.mechanism: a regulatory investigation, which produces documents a journalist could not obtain
tuples.evidence_lens: the regulator's findings compared with the charity's published accounts

tuples.episode_object: a company collapse where the assets were smaller than reported
tuples.time_place_scope: a business whose accounts overstated its holdings
tuples.mechanism: assets that were never there, which is a reporting failure and not a disappearance
tuples.evidence_lens: the administrators' report compared with the audited accounts

tuples.episode_object: the auditor who signed the accounts and the review that followed

tuples.episode_object: the vocalisation identified as a known animal at an unusual time

tuples.episode_object: the museum that accepted a specimen and catalogued it honestly

tuples.episode_object: the researcher who published a negative result and lost funding

tuples.episode_object: the geological assessment that reached a different conclusion

tuples.episode_object: the site whose earliest phase was much older than expected

tuples.episode_object: the alignment claimed to a star position in a distant epoch

tuples.episode_object: the destruction of a site before it could be properly dated

tuples.mechanism: a site lost before analysis, which permanently prevents resolution
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving records compared with the site as it was

tuples.episode_object: the dating technique that was refined and changed several conclusions
tuples.time_place_scope: a period when a method's calibration improved
tuples.mechanism: a recalibration shifting many dates, which is normal and reads as reversal

tuples.episode_object: the case for asking what exactly a date is a date of
tuples.time_place_scope: a methodological point underlying every dispute here

tuples.evidence_lens: the sample descriptions compared with the claims built on them

coverage_profiles.subject: maps that show more than they should

tuples.episode_object: a sixteenth-century chart showing a southern landmass
tuples.time_place_scope: a compilation map drawn from many older sources
tuples.mechanism: a speculative landmass drawn from convention, which is easily read as knowledge

tuples.episode_object: the claim that the chart shows a coastline under ice
tuples.time_place_scope: an interpretation matching an outline to a modern survey
tuples.mechanism: a match between an outline and a survey, which depends entirely on the projection chosen
tuples.evidence_lens: the chart's own projection compared with the modern coastline data

tuples.episode_object: the projection problem that makes such comparisons unreliable
tuples.time_place_scope: a technical issue in comparing old and modern maps
tuples.mechanism: a projection mismatch, which can be made to produce almost any correspondence
tuples.evidence_lens: the chart's construction compared with the modern map used for comparison

tuples.episode_object: the source maps the compiler names in his own legend
tuples.time_place_scope: a chart whose author lists his sources on the map

tuples.evidence_lens: the map's own legend compared with the claims made about it

tuples.episode_object: a portolan chart of exceptional accuracy for its date
tuples.time_place_scope: a Mediterranean navigational tradition of high quality

tuples.episode_object: the compass rose and the practice that produced the accuracy
tuples.time_place_scope: a navigational method using bearings and estimated distances
tuples.mechanism: an ordinary method producing an impressive result, which is the actual story
tuples.evidence_lens: the charts compared with the navigational practice documented

tuples.episode_object: a map showing an island that was later removed from charts
tuples.time_place_scope: a feature carried for a century and then deleted

tuples.episode_object: a map with a coastline drawn before any recorded voyage

tuples.evidence_lens: the paper and ink analysis compared with the claimed date

tuples.episode_object: the watermark evidence that dated a disputed map
tuples.time_place_scope: a physical analysis of the sheet itself
tuples.mechanism: a material date, which settles a dispute about a document
tuples.evidence_lens: the watermark evidence compared with the claimed date of composition

tuples.episode_object: a map annotated by a later hand and read as original
tuples.time_place_scope: a document with additions in a different ink
tuples.mechanism: a later annotation misread as contemporary, which is a common error
tuples.evidence_lens: the ink analysis compared with the reading placed on the annotations

tuples.episode_object: the copy that survives and the original that does not
tuples.time_place_scope: a map known only through later reproductions

tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving copies compared with each other

tuples.episode_object: a chart showing a river system before it was surveyed
tuples.time_place_scope: an interior mapped from indigenous accounts
tuples.mechanism: geographic knowledge obtained by asking, which is the ordinary explanation
tuples.evidence_lens: the chart compared with the explorers' own accounts of their informants

tuples.episode_object: the indigenous knowledge that is rarely credited on the map
tuples.time_place_scope: a survey that depended on local guidance
tuples.mechanism: an uncredited source, which is the real historical finding in many of these cases
tuples.evidence_lens: the expedition journals compared with the published maps

tuples.episode_object: the map that turned out to be a modern forgery on old vellum
tuples.time_place_scope: an object examined after acquisition by an institution
tuples.mechanism: a forgery on genuine material, which defeats a superficial examination
tuples.evidence_lens: the ink analysis compared with the parchment dating

tuples.episode_object: the institution that published the map before the analysis was complete
tuples.time_place_scope: a publication timed for maximum attention
tuples.mechanism: publication preceding verification, which is the recurring institutional failure
tuples.evidence_lens: the publication date compared with the analysis timeline

tuples.episode_object: the chart whose accuracy was overstated in the coverage
tuples.time_place_scope: a map described as more precise than it is
tuples.mechanism: an accuracy claim inflated in reporting, which creates the mystery
tuples.evidence_lens: the chart's actual accuracy compared with the claims made about it

tuples.episode_object: the digitisation that let many charts be compared systematically
tuples.time_place_scope: a modern project imaging a large corpus
tuples.mechanism: a corpus made comparable, which resolves questions that single maps cannot
tuples.evidence_lens: the digitised corpus compared with the claims made about individual sheets

tuples.episode_object: the map read as evidence of a voyage nobody recorded
tuples.time_place_scope: a claim requiring an undocumented expedition
tuples.mechanism: a claim requiring an invisible event, which cannot be tested
tuples.evidence_lens: the claim compared with the shipping and financial records of the period

tuples.episode_object: the case for reading a map as a compilation rather than an observation
tuples.time_place_scope: a methodological point about early cartography
tuples.mechanism: an understanding of how maps were made, which dissolves most of these claims
tuples.evidence_lens: the compilation practices compared with the interpretations offered

coverage_profiles.subject: inscriptions whose authenticity is argued over

tuples.episode_object: a runic stone found by a farmer clearing a field

tuples.mechanism: a find with a plausible modern motive, which is the heart of every such dispute

tuples.time_place_scope: an inscription whose grammar postdates its claimed period
